transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m pretty sure the people on this environmental modeling contract I’ve been working on are tracking my revisions. It looks to me like they’re planting errors in the datasets so it seems like I can’t lead the work.

My wife and some of the junior analysts keep saying it’s probably just version-control mistakes, but… I don’t think that explains all of it.

Besides these concerns about your work being sabotaged, have you noticed any recent periods where your mood has been unusually high, irritable, or energetic—or alternatively, very low or depressed—lasting for a week or more?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed and frustrated about what’s happening at work, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a week where I felt unusually high or full of energy. And I don’t think I’ve been depressed like that either. Mostly just… preoccupied with this situation.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t see. It’s more about what I’m noticing in the work files and the way the data keeps changing.
How long have you been noticing and believing that your colleagues are tampering with your work data—days, weeks, or months?
It’s been… about two months, I’d say. That’s when I really started feeling sure they were tracking my revisions and putting errors into the data.
Aside from this situation at work, how have things been going for you overall—are you still able to manage your daily responsibilities, relationships, and self-care as well as before this started?

Not as well as before, no. I’ve gotten pretty far behind on the modeling work, to the point that the firm reassigned parts of the contract away from me. And I’m supposed to be helping the junior analysts, but lately I don’t think I’ve been much use to them.

At home I mostly keep to myself. My wife has had to push me to keep up with basic things, routines and that. So… I’m managing some of it, but not like I was.

Have you noticed any changes in how you think or express yourself—like trouble organizing your thoughts, jumping between unrelated topics, or others telling you that your speech or behavior seems unusual or hard to follow?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been more distracted and stressed, but I haven’t had people telling me I’m not making sense or that I’m jumping around. I feel like I can explain myself clearly enough.

Before these beliefs about your work data started two months ago, had you already been noticing yourself becoming more withdrawn, less motivated, or having trouble keeping up with responsibilities for some time—say, in the months leading up to that?

Yes… I think that had been happening before the work data thing got bad. I was already pulling back some.

I can sit for hours at my desk and not really start anything. Or I’ll be out in the garage with the telescope still covered, even though I used to look forward to astronomy nights. I used to hike more, and I liked mentoring the younger analysts, but lately I just don’t feel much drive to do it or to talk to people. It’s not that I decided to stop. I just… don’t feel the pull like I used to.

Thinking back, how long ago did you first start noticing this pulling back—losing interest in things like astronomy or hiking and feeling less drive to connect with people? Was it more like one month before the work concerns started, or closer to six months or longer?

It was longer than six months. Looking back, I think it really started after I was put in charge of that bigger environmental modeling contract… so about two years and a couple months ago. That’s when I first started noticing I was pulling back and losing steam.

Have you or your wife noticed that your facial expressions or emotional reactions seem more flat or muted than before—like you show less emotion, even in situations that used to make you happy, sad, or excited?

Yeah… I think maybe that’s fair. I don’t know if my face looks different, but I know I don’t react the way I used to. Things like astronomy nights or hiking used to get me excited, and mentoring the younger analysts used to feel good. Now I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered, and I just don’t feel much push to start anything or talk to anyone. My wife has noticed I seem kind of… muted, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a persistent persecutory delusion (colleagues sabotaging his data) lasting 2 months, meeting Criterion A for psychosis. This is preceded by over 2 years of prodromal negative symptoms—avolition, anhedonia, social withdrawal, and blunted/flat affect—confirmed by both patient and spouse observation. No hallucinations, disorganized speech, or catatonic behavior were present, but negative symptoms alone can satisfy Criterion A when prominent. Total symptom duration exceeds 6 months (continuous disturbance since prodrome began), with clear functional decline (loss of contract responsibilities, inability to mentor junior staff, withdrawal from spouse and hobbies). Mood episode was explicitly ruled out, excluding schizoaffective disorder, and the extended prodromal/negative symptom course exceeding 1 month rules out brief psychotic disorder. This pattern is most consistent with Schizophrenia (F20.9).
